deals.handout: West has a game forcing hand with 5 hearts. After the 1 NT rebid, he uses new minor forcing to find a heart fit. East's 2♥ bid shows a minimum with 3 hearts.

problems.explanation: Partner's 1NT shows 12–14 and may include three hearts. You have five hearts and 12 HCP, enough for game. Bid the new minor, 2♣: it's artificial and forcing, and asks whether partner has three hearts.

whyNot.3N: Partner may have three hearts, making a 5-3 fit. Ask with 2♣ first.
whyNot.4H: Partner may have only two hearts. Ask with 2♣ first.
whyNot.2H: Rebidding 2♥ is weak: partner will pass. You have game values.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2♣ is new minor forcing: do you have three hearts, and how strong are you? You have three hearts and a minimum (12–13), so bid 2♥.

whyNot.3H: Jumping to 3♥ shows three hearts and a maximum (13–14). With 13 you're at the bottom of that; the handout calls this a minimum.
whyNot.2N: Show three-card support for partner's major first.
whyNot.2D: Rebidding your suit comes last, when nothing else fits. You have three hearts.

problems.explanation: Partner has three hearts, so you have a 5-3 fit, and your 2♣ promised game values. Bid 4♥.

whyNot.3N: You've found an eight-card heart fit. Play in hearts.
whyNot.3H: Your new minor bid was forcing to game. Bid it.

deals.handout: South has an invitational hand with 5 spades. He bids NMF to show this and search for a fit. North jumps to 3 NT to show a maximum without any extra major suit length.

problems.explanation: You have five spades and 11 HCP: enough to invite. Partner's 1NT may include three spades. After a 1♥ opening both minors are new, so bid your better one, 2♣, as new minor forcing.

whyNot.2S: Rebidding 2♠ is weak: partner will pass. You have enough to invite.
whyNot.2N: 2NT invites, but could miss a 5-3 spade fit. Ask with 2♣ first.
whyNot.3S: A jump to 3♠ shows six spades. You have five.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2♣ is new minor forcing. You have only two spades, and a maximum (14) with diamonds stopped. Jump to 3NT: no spade fit, and the top of your range.

whyNot.2N: 2NT shows a minimum. With 14, jump to 3NT.
whyNot.2S: Showing spades promises three. You have two.
whyNot.2H: Rebidding hearts comes last, when nothing else fits. With a maximum and a diamond stopper, bid notrump.

deals.handout: East has a game forcing hand with 5 hearts and uses NMF to find a fit. West jumps to 3♥ to show extras with 3 hearts. East bids game.

problems.explanation: You have five hearts and 12 HCP, enough for game. Partner's 1NT may include three hearts. Bid the new minor, 2♦, to ask.

whyNot.3N: Partner may have three hearts. Ask with 2♦ first.
whyNot.4H: Partner may have only two hearts. Ask with 2♦ first.
whyNot.2H: Rebidding 2♥ is weak: partner will pass. You have game values.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2♦ is new minor forcing. You have three hearts and a maximum (14), so jump to 3♥.

whyNot.2H: 2♥ shows three hearts but a minimum. You have 14: jump.
whyNot.2N: Show three-card support for partner's major first.
whyNot.3D: Raising the new minor comes after showing heart support. You have three hearts.

problems.explanation: Partner has three hearts and a maximum. You have the 5-3 fit and game values: bid 4♥.

whyNot.3N: You've found an eight-card heart fit. Play in hearts.
whyNot.P: Your 2♦ promised game values. Bid game.

deals.handout: South has a strong invitational hand with 5-4 in the majors. He uses NMF over partner's 1 NT rebid. North shows 3 spades and a minimum but South tries once more in vain.

problems.explanation: You have five spades, four hearts and 11 HCP. Bid the new minor, 2♦: partner shows four hearts first, then three spades. Bidding 2♥ yourself wouldn't be forcing.

whyNot.2H: After a 1NT rebid, 2♥ isn't forcing, or even invitational. With a good hand, use new minor forcing.
whyNot.2N: 2NT could miss a 4-4 heart fit or a 5-3 spade fit. Ask with 2♦.

problems.explanation: Partner's 2♦ is new minor forcing. You don't have four hearts, but you have three spades and a minimum (12–13), so bid 2♠.

whyNot.3S: Jumping shows three spades and a maximum (13–14). The handout treats this as a minimum.
whyNot.2H: Showing hearts promises four. You have three.
whyNot.2N: Show three-card support for partner's major first.

acceptable.P: Partner has shown a minimum, so stopping in 2♠ is reasonable too. The handout tries once more.

problems.explanation: Partner has three spades and a minimum. With 11 HCP and a good 5-4 shape, invite once more with 3♠: partner bids game with anything extra.

whyNot.4S: Partner has shown a minimum. Invite and let partner decide.

problems.explanation: Partner invited again, but you've already shown a minimum and have nothing more to add. Pass.

whyNot.4S: You have a minimum, which you've already shown. Decline.

deals.handout: With an invitational hand without 5 hearts South does not use NMF.

problems.explanation: New minor forcing looks for a 5-3 fit in your major, so it needs five cards. You have four hearts, and partner's 1NT rebid denied four. With 11 HCP, invite game with 2NT.

whyNot.2C: New minor forcing needs a five-card major. You have four hearts, and partner has already denied four.
whyNot.3N: 11 HCP opposite 12–14 is only enough to invite.
whyNot.2H: Rebidding hearts shows five or more, and partner will pass. You have four.

problems.explanation: Partner invited with 2NT. You have 13 HCP and a good five-card diamond suit: accept.

whyNot.P: With 13 and a five-card suit, you're worth accepting.

deals.handout: With a minimum game forcing hand with 6 spades South should bid game. There is no need to use NMF since South already knows
reviewNotes: The handout says South should bid game; West bid 4♠. The handout's sentence is also cut off.

problems.explanation: Partner's 1NT promises at least two spades, so with six spades you already know there's an eight-card fit. You have 13 HCP: bid game. New minor forcing would only ask a question you know the answer to.

whyNot.2D: New minor forcing asks about three-card support. With six spades you know there's a fit already.
whyNot.3S: A jump to 3♠ only invites. With 13 HCP opposite an opener, bid game.
whyNot.3N: You have six spades and partner at least two: play in spades.
